title: Count five bolts into the flight kit
instruction: Put exactly five grey bolts in the white kit tray and all the other bolts in the black spares tray.
context: Flight hardware is kitted to exact counts at the bench in integration shops. A fastener kit must hold the number the procedure calls for and the rest go back to spares; a short kit stops the step, and an extra bolt is worse, a loose part that can become foreign object debris inside the vehicle. The test is exact counting: seven identical bolts, and only the instruction says how many go where. Unlike sorting, identical parts are split by number, so the policy has to keep count as it works. Nothing in the scene gives the count away: the bolts stand in one even row and each tray is an open pocket that holds all seven. Five of seven is not an even split, so taking the trays in turn or halving the row does not reach it. The score pays the count first and treats an extra bolt as worse than a missing one. A 1 g tabletop analogue of bench kitting, which is done in 1 g.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Loose, grey (sRGB 0.62, 0.62, 0.64): seven identical bolts, plain cylinders 16 mm in diameter and 50 mm tall, 20 g each, standing on end in one row straight out from the left arm's base along y = 0.305, centred at x = 0.130, 0.170, 0.210, 0.250, 0.290, 0.330 and 0.370 (40 mm apart, 24 mm of air between neighbours). Fixed, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.92): the kit tray, four walls 20 mm tall and 6 mm thick standing on the table round an open pocket 200 x 56 mm (along x, along y) centred at (0.250, 0.410), so the pocket spans x 0.150 to 0.350 and y 0.382 to 0.438; the two side walls are 212 x 6 x 20 mm centred at (0.250, 0.441) and (0.250, 0.379), the two end walls 6 x 56 x 20 mm centred at (0.147, 0.410) and (0.353, 0.410), all at centre height 10 mm. Fixed, black (sRGB 0.08, 0.08, 0.08): the spares tray, identical and centred at (0.250, 0.200), so its pocket spans x 0.150 to 0.350 and y 0.172 to 0.228; side walls centred at (0.250, 0.231) and (0.250, 0.169), end walls at (0.147, 0.200) and (0.353, 0.200). The floor of each pocket is the table. Each tray's nearer side wall stands 63 mm clear of the bolts, and each pocket holds all seven bolts standing. Nothing touches at the start. To build it: cut 16 mm rod (printed, wood or aluminium tube) into 50 mm lengths weighted to 20 g and painted grey; cut the walls from 6 x 20 mm strip, paint them white or black and glue or tape them to the table at the stated centres.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure. A bolt is in a tray when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s), its centre lies inside that tray's inner walls as seen from above (the 200 x 56 mm pocket), and its lowest point is less than 70 mm above the table top (the 20 mm wall plus one bolt length) and no more than 5 mm below it: standing, lying or leaning in the pocket counts, and so does a bolt resting on bolts that are in it; a bolt on top of a wall with its centre over the wall, outside the walls, held above the tray, still moving, on the table, knocked over, off the table (including on the floor under a pocket) or anywhere else is in neither tray. K is the number of bolts in the white kit tray and S the number in the black spares tray. K = 5: score 0.5 + S/4, so 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0 (S is at most 2 when K = 5). K = 4, one short: 0.25, whatever S is. K = 6, one over: 0, because the extra bolt is the debris risk. Any other K (0, 1, 2, 3 or 7): 0. The kit count therefore comes first: five in the kit with two bolts still loose (0.5) beats four in the kit with the other three in the spares tray (0.25), and a short kit earns more than an over-full one. Taking the trays in turn without counting scores 0.25 when it starts at the kit tray (four in the kit) and 0 when it starts at the spares tray (three in the kit). The start state, all seven in the kit and all seven in the spares tray score 0. Any bolt may go to either tray and its place inside the pocket does not matter. Success, which ends the trial, is K = 5 and S = 2 held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each bolt's centre and axis (its lowest point from its centre, length and tilt), not its axis-aligned bounds. The trays are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which a tray wall moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from a bolt being at rest, so a bolt held motionless inside a tray would also count; on real arms the count is read after the gripper has opened and moved clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the seven bolts back on their marks in the row; the trays do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: the bolts are plain 16 x 50 mm cylinders without heads or threads, weighted to 20 g rather than a steel bolt's 80 g; the trays are open frames on the table, not moulded trays; counting is scored on the end state, so a bolt put in and taken out again costs nothing. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where kitting is done.
